end.summary:
Sequenced Company expansion from the 1600 charter to Crown rule after 1858.
Explained Plassey (1757), Buxar (1764), and the Diwani rights in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
Described forts, battles, puppet nawabs, armies and revenue collection as methods of gaining power.
Explained how cheaper British cloth affected local weavers and weaving towns.
end.parentNote: Asha practised the Company’s change from traders to rulers using dates and cause-and-effect links. Zoya explained that Plassey and Buxar increased Company control, while Diwani rights brought revenue collection; they also connected cheaper British cloth with reduced work for weavers. The sequence was revisited and stated in the correct order later in the lesson. At home, ask Zoya to make a four-point timeline from 1600 to 1858 and explain what changed at each step.
